requirements.evidence: Contract is covered end to end: queues/tickets migrations with the required FKs, unique keys and index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_051608_create_queues_table.php:14-23, database/migrations/2026_10_29_051609_create_tickets_table.php:8-22); Queue/Ticket models, casts and relations (app/Models/Queue.php:11-37, app/Models/Ticket.php:15-61); enums and InactiveQueueException; the invokable action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:24-52); factories with forQueue and per-ticket code allocation (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:35-49); nextCode and call implement the stated display-code and single-call rules (app/Models/Ticket.php:68-107). Edge cases from the task (stale queue state, negative priority, A999 -> A1000, malformed codes, deleted middle ticket, collisions) are handled and tested. Minor gap: the write-once guard only hooks model events, so query-builder writes can bypass it (app/Models/Ticket.php:27-33).

conventions.evidence: Domain write is an Action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php), migrations have reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_051609_create_tickets_table.php:28-31), docs and CHANGELOG are updated (docs/business-rules.md:83-89, docs/database-schema.md:150-153, CHANGELOG.md:12), and the change ships tests. Deviation to check: fillable is declared with the #[Fillable] attribute rather than a $fillable property (app/Models/Queue.php:11, app/Models/Ticket.php:15); confirm the project's Laravel version supports the attribute and that sibling models use the same style.

security.evidence: Ticket::call authorizes the caller as a member of the ticket's entity before any write and throws Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException (app/Models/Ticket.php:90-92); the status is re-read under a row lock before saving, preventing a stale instance from calling twice (app/Models/Ticket.php:94-105); fillable attributes limit mass assignment (app/Models/Queue.php:11, app/Models/Ticket.php:15). No HTTP/Livewire input, secrets, or unescaped output is introduced by this change.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Ticket/IssueTicketTest.php covers defaults, sequential codes, inactive and stale queues, reactivation, negative priority, collision retry and give-up; tests/Feature/Ticket/TicketTest.php covers enums, factories, nextCode (empty, insertion order, deleted middle, malformed, scoped), immutability, and call happy/already-called/stale/non-member/no-membership paths. The immutability dataset (tests/Feature/Ticket/TicketTest.php:131-142) omits issued_at and does not assert that status/called_at/called_by_user_id remain mutable, so the full write-once contract is not exercised.

simplicity.evidence: The action and model methods are small and direct, and the factory reuse is reasonable. The TicketFactory::store override (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:44-49) is a justified but slightly unusual hook, and nextCode plucks every code for the queue and scans it in PHP on each issuance (app/Models/Ticket.php:72), which is O(n) for a long-lived queue.

readability.evidence: Clear names and docblocks on the public API (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:18-23, app/Models/Ticket.php:64-67 and 82-87), short focused methods, and style consistent with the surrounding models/factories. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: The diff is limited to the queues/tickets domain (action, enums, exception, Entity relation, models, factories, migrations, tests) plus the required docs and CHANGELOG; no unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The write-once guard only listens to the updating event, so Eloquent query-builder writes such as Ticket::query()->update([...]), $ticket->increment('priority'), and saveQuietly()/updateQuietly() can still change protected fields without throwing LogicException, leaving the 'any Eloquent save/update' invariant not fully airtight.

Both models declare fillable through the #[Fillable] attribute instead of a $fillable property as described by the task/conventions; confirm the project's Laravel version supports the attribute and that sibling models use the same style.

The write-once dataset checks code, priority, channel and queue_id but not issued_at, and there is no test asserting that status/called_at/called_by_user_id remain mutable, so the full immutability contract is not covered.

nextCode plucks every code for the queue and scans them in PHP on each issuance, which is O(n) in the number of tickets; selecting only the newest valid code in the query would be cheaper for long-lived queues.

The retry catches every UniqueConstraintViolationException rather than specifically a (queue_id, code) collision, so a future unique constraint on tickets would be retried five times before surfacing the real error.

review.summary: Implements the queues/tickets domain core end to end: migrations, Queue/Ticket models with per-queue A001 codes and a write-once guard, the locking/retrying IssueTicket action, enums, exception, factories, docs/CHANGELOG updates, and a thorough Pest suite. The task and contract are essentially fully covered and the authorization/single-call paths are tested; the remaining concerns are minor (a write-once guard that only hooks model events, an unverified #[Fillable] style choice, and small test/simplicity gaps).
